title: The delete gate does not read a data heredoc's body as a command
intention: bin/cmd/deletegate removes the body of every here-document whose command is a data writer (cat or tee, optionally with redirects) before asking its two questions; a here-document fed to anything else (bash, sh, python, eval, ssh, ...) is kept and judged as today; the co-occurrence trade is otherwise unchanged.
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. This ticket closes live trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/deletegate-refuses-by-co-occurrence-across-clauses.json, a measured fault that enters as a bug (skills/intent/SKILL.md: a bug enters as a ticket, not through /intent). Measured 2026-10-08, n>=5: a `cat >> ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md <<'EOF'` whose prose contains the word rm is refused; the same append without the word is allowed; scratchpad probe scripts whose text mentions both are refused.
traces_to: Law 7 / CP4 (a gate whose false refusals cost more than a retype stops serving the work); Law 9 (measurement, n>=5, settles the trade the docstring recorded at n=2).
how: bin/cmd/deletegate verdict() (:110): before DESTRUCTIVE.search, strip data heredoc bodies with one regex pass: for each `<<-?\s*['"]?(\w+)['"]?` whose preceding command word on that line is cat or tee, drop the lines up to the matching terminator. Update the docstring's trade paragraph with the 2026-10-08 measurement and this narrowing, keeping the rest of the trade verbatim.
